steps.title: The same root, poured into a different pattern
body: A root can be poured into more than one verb pattern, not just Form I's bare فَعَلَ. Nine more patterns — Forms II through X — build related but distinct verbs from the same three consonants, each with its own shape and its own tendency of meaning. This is the same root-and-pattern idea from root & pattern, applied to verbs instead of nouns.

Form II's signature is a doubled middle root consonant — a shaddah on the second radical — giving the shape فَعَّلَ. جَرَّبَ ("to try / to try on"), already in your vocabulary since A2, is a Form II verb: جَرَّبَ, present tense يُجَرِّبُ.

Form II most often adds a causative or intensive sense to a Form I verb, or turns a noun/adjective directly into a verb (a denominative). جَرَّبَ itself has no everyday Form I "جَرَبَ" behind it — the pattern's tendency still holds even when the "paired" plain form isn't a common word, a warning worth keeping for every form ahead.

steps.title: Form II in one sentence
steps.intro: Read the sentence, then check what marks it as Form II. Tap 🔊 to hear it.

steps.title: Spot the pattern
steps.prompt: جَرَّبَ (to try) has a doubled middle letter. Which form is that?
steps.explanation: فَعَّلَ doubles the middle root letter (the shaddah on the ر in جَرَّبَ) — the mark of Form II.

steps.title: Meaning tendency
steps.prompt: What does Form II most often add to a Form I verb's meaning?

options.label: A causative or intensive sense — "to make X happen" or "to X thoroughly"
A reciprocal sense — doing the action with someone
Something happening on its own, with no one performing it

steps.explanation: Form II's doubled middle consonant most often causes or intensifies the Form I meaning. The reciprocal sense belongs to Form III, and the "no one performing it" sense belongs to Form VII — both still ahead.

steps.title: You've met your first derived verb form
steps.message: Form II — doubled middle consonant, often causative or intensive. Seven more forms are ahead, most already hiding in verbs you know.
